newsitem.title: UK: Royal Bank of Scotland lifts full year profits.
newsitem.headline: Royal Bank of Scotland lifts full year profits.

text.p: Royal Bank of Scotland on Thursday said its full year pretax profits rose by 15 percent 695.0 million pounds ($1.17 billion) with strong growth in its UK and U.S. banking operations offsetting a dip at its insurance unit.

Royal Bank said its U.S. bank Citizens, based in New England, lifted profits by 61 million pounds, or 57 percent, adding that it will continue its strategy of deepening its franchise and expanding its core business.
Profits were also higher in UK Banking, up 97 million pounds or 22 percent, and this part of the business also showed a healthy improvement in cost-to-income ratio.
The latter fell to 59.2 percent from 63.2 percent while the group ratio was down to 50 percent from 51.7 percent.
Direct Line, which sells motor, house and life insurance, saw profits shrink by 86 million pounds to 26 million for the year as premium rates continued ander pressure and it saw increased claims.
The Royal Bank figures included a 72 million pound gain from the sale of an interest in a German bank and a cost of 21 million pounds from restructuring an acquisition by Citizens.
Royal Bank chairman Lord Younger said the bank is well placed to develop its competitive position.
"Our banking businesses in the UK and U.S. are set to expand profitability, while Direct Line will benefit once motor premium rates recover," Younger said in a statement. ($1=.5956 Pound)
